'''''Lonchidionoides''''' is an extinct [[genus]] of [[hybodont]] in the family [[Lonchidiidae]]. The genus contains a [[Monotypic taxon|single named species]], '''''Lonchidionoides trifurcatum''''', known from the 'mid'-Cretaceous (latest [[Albian]]–early [[Cenomanian]] ages) [[Tiout Formation]] of Algeria. Teeth of this genus are also known from the [[Early Cretaceous]] ([[Barremian]]–[[Aptian]] ages) [[Quiricó Formation]] of Brazil, and have been left in open nomenclature as ''L''. sp. pending new material.<ref name="vulloetal2026">{{Cite journal |last=Vullo |first=Romain |last2=Fragoso |first2=Léo Galvão Carnier |last3=Bittencourt |first3=Jonathas S. |last4=Pérez-García |first4=Adán |last5=Bouchemla |first5=Imad |last6=Benyoucef |first6=Madani |date=2026 |title=A new genus of lonchidiid hybodontiform sharks from the Cretaceous of North Africa and South America |journal=Geological Magazine |language=en |volume=163 |doi=10.1017/S0016756825100484 |issn=0016-7568}}</ref>

== Discovery and naming ==
[[File:Lonchidionoides localities.png|thumb|left|Localities where ''Lonchidionoides'' teeth have been found]]

In 2026, Romain Vullo and colleagues described ''Lonchidionoides trifurcatum'' as a new genus and species of lonchidiid hybodont based on five teeth from the [[Tiout Formation]] ('Garet El Hemmam' locality) of [[Laghouat Province]], northern Algeria. The [[Genus|generic name]], ''Lonchidionodes'', derives from its similarity to the teeth of ''[[Lonchidion]]'', the namesake of the family Lonchidiidae. The [[Specific name (zoology)|specific name]], ''trifurcatum'', refers to the [[trident]]-like morphology of the anterior dentition.<ref name="vulloetal2026" />

Nine isolated teeth from the Early [[Cretaceous]] [[Quiricó Formation]] ('Fazenda Tereza' locality) were initially described as ?Lonchidiidae in 2021.<ref name="fragosoetal2021">{{cite journal |last1=Fragoso |first1=Léo Galvão Carnier |last2=Bittencourt |first2=Jonathas S. |last3=Mateus |first3=Ana Luisa D |last4=Cozzuol |first4=Mario Alberto |last5=Richter |first5=Martha |title=Shark (Chondrichthyes) microremains from the Lower Cretaceous Quiricó Formation, Sanfranciscana Basin, Southeast Brazil |journal=Historical Biology |date=2021 |volume=33 |issue=8 |pages=1308–1316 |doi=10.1080/08912963.2019.1692830}}</ref> These are nearly identical in morphology and size to ''L. trifurcatum'', but remain in open nomenclature as ''L.'' sp., awaiting further specimens that would allow more precise taxonomy.<ref name="vulloetal2026" />
